thread:
ci-bot: nightly-perf-alert: jobs/prod-serving/nightly-dashboard reported p95 latency +28% vs baseline for kernel-selector path across canary pool. Alert id: perf-1992304000
alex: saw the alert, digging into the trace buckets now. looks like kernel switch counts jumped at 02:12 UTC.
priya: are we sure it's kernel-selector? could be batching heuristics changing the sequence-length distribution. any related merges today?
sam: quick grep in changelog: merge MR #4821 'adaptive-kernel-threshold' landed ~01:45 UTC from raj.
raj: yeah that was my change — small refactor to selector epsilon and a new fastpath for sequence < 64. I added unit tests and perf smoke locally, passed.
ops-jen: CI shows a perf check failure on the canary suite at 02:08 but the merge went through because the flaky check marked as non-blocking. attaching CI snippet.
ops-jen: ```
=== perf-check summary ===
canary/p95: baseline 42ms -> current 55ms (+31%)
kv-miss-rate: 0.21 -> 0.62
batching-window-mean: 3.2ms -> 1.1ms
=== end ===
```
priya: kv-miss-rate jump + batching-window shrink — that smells like the selector promoted a path that disables prefix/KV reuse when it switches kernels mid-seq.
alex: I profiled a sample request with `perf-trace --req 0x7f...` and saw frequent KV rehydrations and L2 cache thrash. stack snippet:
```
kernel_selector::choose_for(seq_len=120) -> fastpath(seq<64) mismatch -> recompile -> fallback_kernel
kv_cache::evict_prefetchers() called 8x more per-request
```
sam: rolling back MR #4821 locally restores baseline on my repro. can we do a quick revert in prod canary?
raj: on it. opened MR #4829 revert adaptive-kernel-threshold.
ops-jen: deploying revert to canary now, will monitor dashboard. ETA ~8m.
ci-bot: deploy: canary revert MR #4829 started by raj.
priya: after revert, initial 10min window looks better: p95 back to ~44ms, kv-miss-rate down to 0.23. good signal.
alex: plan: 1) keep revert in canary until we have test covering cross-seq-kernel transitions 2) add a regression test that simulates seq_len drift and ensures KV reuse invariants 3) rework threshold logic to consult running kv-hit heuristics before switching kernels.
sam: I'll open follow-up MR with test harness and a gating perf check. tagging @priya for review.
ops-jen: note for postmortem: make the canary perf-check blocking for kernel-selector changes. too many silent regressions recently.
raj: sorry everyone, I'll prioritize a less aggressive fastpath and add telemetry. thanks for catching quickly. :thanks: 
ci-bot: alert cleared: perf-1992304000 resolved (revert confirmed on canary).
